title: Smile
text:
For Tatiana, my first daughter


The day is gray
and my hands are cold
when through the
        window
I see the rosebushes shaking
in the garden
lashed by the
        wind.
It begins to rain
like a slow apprenticeship
of
        nature
until the darkness
that has been growing
enters
        my spirit.
I hear a slight
sigh
behind me
and I
        turn around
seeking to recover the time
of joy
in the exact
        space
occupied by the small
animated bundle
on the rug.

        In her pale face I see myself repeated
and I think that smile of hers

        innocent
is capable of moving the world
in which I move

        lighting it
until it clips the wings
of sadness
and restores
        a thousand times
the genuine face
of peace.
editorial_note: The translation preserves the poem's domestic turn from gray weather into the child's restorative smile.

title: You Do Not Even
text:
You do not even

deserve an

epigram
editorial_note: The translation keeps Cardenal's miniature rebuke stripped down to its three-line refusal.

title: You Came to Visit Me
text:
You came to visit me

in dreams


but the emptiness

you left when

you went away


was reality
editorial_note: The translation preserves the contrast between the dream visit and the real emptiness afterward.

title: The Person
text:
The person

closest

to me


is you

the one

whom, however,


I have not seen

for so long


except in dreams.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the poem's slow revelation that nearness survives only in dream.

title: The Heavy Ones
text:
The heavy

drops seem like


someone climbing

the step


and the wind striking

the door


a woman

about to come in.
editorial_note: The translation keeps the rain and wind as the imagined arrival of a woman at the door.
